@{64873f159cf028090ce2c2e2|full_name}: Right now a sort of similar issue is going on where outdated information is showing for some people in the social menu that doesn't get updated until you view their profile in the main menu.

For instance, I had one friend the other night that was showing up as orange in the quick menu friend's wing, but when I brought them up in the main menu, their status *immediately* changed to green and showed them as being in an open lobby. This happens with multiple friends.

I found that there are two different variations of this bug. One is more common, where socials (players' locations, status, and thumbnail) continue updating but at an irregular rate, and sometimes only updating individual players when triggered manually by clicking through to their page.

The other is more severe, where at some point socials will stop updating entirely and invites are no longer received in game. Socials and invites remain broken until restarting the game, which also requires logging in again. In this case it is related to this IPv6 issue and can be worked around with some of the solutions discussed here: https://feedback.vrchat.com/bug-reports/p/restart-to-receive-invites

It seems that the post has not been updated quite often, but as of April 2025, I am experiencing this issue in my environment too. The Social is not updating at all and remains as it was when I logged in. Even when I confirm my friends' online status on the VRC web, they still appear as "offline" in Social. When I open that friend's bio from Social, it does show the correct status, however this friend will disappear from my friend list until I restart the game.

Yes, I've read and checked with the IPv6 thing.. but I cant do anything with it because I am on Pico4 android, and no such settings.

After that, I conducted various experiments on my own. It seems that the issue is definitely related to IPv6 processing. In the PICO4 standalone, there are no settings to disalbe IPv6, but the problem was RESOLVED by routing through a server that blocks IPv6. More specifically, I created a local DNS and routed through it. This method is not a solution that anyone can easily implement, but I believe it proves that the issue was indeed caused by IPv6. I have not confirmed any other drawbacks from using this method. Therefore, I would like to suggest the developers to consider making a fix based on this approach.
